description:
## Goal Implement `Filament.Test` — the Rung 2 test API for mounting and driving a single Filament component in isolation. No WebSocket, no real browser. Observable dependencies are replaced with stubs (from F4). State updates triggered by event handlers are processed synchronously. This is the primary API used by Track H (tests) and Track G (examples-as-tests). ## Deviation policy Any deviation from this spec requires prior approval. Stop work, run `bw comment "..."` describing the conflict, reopen the ticket, and await guidance. Do not improvise. --- ## Prerequisites All of the following must be merged before starting: - Track B (flm-t8j — all closed ✓) — Filament.Fiber, Filament.Reconciler, Filament.Renderer - Track C (flm-oue — all closed ✓) — Filament.Hooks, Filament.RenderContext - Track D D4 (flm-hom.4) — use_observable/3 - Track E E3 (flm-zoc.3) — event handler dispatch - F4 (this epic) — Filament.Test.Stub, observable_stubs in RenderContext Check the following module APIs before implementing (they were built in those tracks and this ticket must interoperate with them exactly as built): - `Filament.Reconciler.mount/2` or `mount/3` — check its actual signature in `lib/filament/reconciler.ex`. The spec in B6's ticket proposed returning `{tree, rendered, pending_effects}` but may differ. Read the file. - `Filament.Reconciler.update/3` or `update/4` — same caveat. - `Filament.FiberTree.update_hook_slot/4` — from D4 - `Filament.FiberTree.get_event_handler/3` — from E3 If any of these signatures differ from expectations, adapt this ticket's implementation to match what is actually there. If the discrepancy is severe, stop and comment. --- ## 1. Filament.Test module FILE: test/support/filament_test.ex (or lib/filament/test.ex — follow mix.exs convention) ### TestView struct ```elixir defmodule Filament.Test do @moduledoc """ Rung 2 test API for Filament components. Mount a component in isolation, drive it with simulated events, assert on rendered HTML. No WebSocket required. Example: import Filament.Test {:ok, stub} = Filament.Test.Stub.start(fn _ -> %{count: 0} end) {:ok, view} = mount(Counter, %{server: stub}) assert render_text(view) =~ "Count: 0" {:ok, view} = click(view, "button") assert render_text(view) =~ "Count: 1" """ defstruct [ :component, # module — the component under test :props, # map — initial props :fiber_tree, # %Filament.FiberTree{} — current fiber state :rendered, # %Phoenix.LiveView.Rendered{} — last render output :rendered_html, # String.t() — rendered_html as a plain string :owner_pid, # pid() — always self() at mount time :stubs # %{server_id => pid()} — stub map from F4 ] @type t :: %__MODULE__{} ``` ### mount/3 ```elixir @doc """ Mount `component` with `props`. Returns {:ok, view} or {:error, reason}. Options: :stub — list of {server_identity, stub_fn} pairs (see Filament.Test.Stub). Example: stub: [{CartServer, fn _req -> %{items: []} end}] """ @spec mount(component :: module(), props :: map(), opts :: keyword()) :: {:ok, t()} | {:error, term()} def mount(component, props, opts \\ []) do stub_specs = Keyword.get(opts, :stub, []) {stubs_map, _pids} = Filament.Test.Stub.build(stub_specs) owner_pid = self() case Filament.Reconciler.mount(component, props, %{ owner_pid: owner_pid, observable_stubs: stubs_map }) do {:ok, fiber_tree, rendered} -> html = rendered_to_string(rendered) view = %__MODULE__{ component: component, props: props, fiber_tree: fiber_tree, rendered: rendered, rendered_html: html, owner_pid: owner_pid, stubs: stubs_map } {:ok, flush_messages(view)} {:error, reason} -> {:error, reason} end end ``` NOTE on Reconciler.mount/3: If the actual signature uses different argument names or returns a different tuple shape, adapt accordingly. The intent is: mount the component, get back a fiber tree and rendered output. The third argument carries context including owner_pid and observable_stubs — check how B6/B7 and C1 thread these through and match that pattern. ### rendered_to_string/1 ```elixir @doc false def rendered_to_string(%Phoenix.LiveView.Rendered{static: static, dynamic: dynamic}) do parts = dynamic.(false) # false = initial render (not a diff update) interleave(static, parts) |> IO.iodata_to_binary() end defp interleave([s | statics], [d | dynamics]) do [s, part_to_iodata(d) | interleave(statics, dynamics)] end defp interleave([s], []), do: [s] defp interleave([], []), do: [] defp part_to_iodata(nil), do: "" defp part_to_iodata(s) when is_binary(s), do: s defp part_to_iodata({:safe, data}), do: data defp part_to_iodata(%Phoenix.LiveView.Rendered{} = r), do: rendered_to_string(r) defp part_to_iodata(other), do: Phoenix.HTML.Engine.encode_to_iodata!(other) ``` ### render_text/1 ```elixir @doc "Return the rendered HTML as a plain string (with HTML tags stripped)." @spec render_text(t()) :: String.t() def render_text(%__MODULE__{rendered_html: html}) do html |> Floki.parse_fragment!() |> Floki.text() |> String.trim() end ``` ### has_class?/3 ```elixir @doc """ Return true if the element matching `selector` has CSS class `class_name`. Raises if selector matches no elements. """ @spec has_class?(t(), selector :: String.t(), class_name :: String.t()) :: boolean() def has_class?(%__MODULE__{rendered_html: html}, selector, class_name) do html |> Floki.parse_fragment!() |> Floki.find(selector) |> case do [] -> raise "has_class?: no element matched selector #{inspect(selector)}" elements -> Enum.any?(elements, fn el -> class_attr = Floki.attribute(el, "class") |> List.first() || "" class_name in String.split(class_attr, ~r/\s+/, trim: true) end) end end ``` ### click/2 ```elixir @doc """ Simulate a click on the element matching `selector`. Finds the phx-click attribute, dispatches the event handler, flushes resulting state updates, and re-renders. Returns {:ok, updated_view} or {:error, reason}. """ @spec click(t(), selector :: String.t()) :: {:ok, t()} | {:error, term()} def click(%__MODULE__{} = view, selector) do case find_event_ref(view.rendered_html, selector, "phx-click") do {:ok, ref} -> dispatch_event(view, ref, %{}) {:error, _} = err -> err end end ``` ### submit/3 ```elixir @doc """ Simulate a form submission on the element matching `selector` with `params`. Finds the phx-submit attribute on the form, dispatches the handler with params, flushes state updates, re-renders. Returns {:ok, updated_view} or {:error, reason}. """ @spec submit(t(), selector :: String.t(), params :: map()) :: {:ok, t()} | {:error, term()} def submit(%__MODULE__{} = view, selector, params \\ %{}) do case find_event_ref(view.rendered_html, selector, "phx-submit") do {:ok, ref} -> dispatch_event(view, ref, params) {:error, _} = err -> err end end ``` ### Private helpers ```elixir defp find_event_ref(html, selector, attr) do html |> Floki.parse_fragment!() |> Floki.find(selector) |> case do [] -> {:error, {:no_element, selector}} elements -> case Floki.attribute(elements, attr) do [] -> {:error, {:no_attribute, attr, selector}} [ref | _] -> {:ok, ref} end end end defp dispatch_event(view, "filament:" <> ref, params) do case String.split(ref, ":", parts: 2) do [fiber_id_str, index_str] -> handler_index = String.to_integer(index_str) handler = Filament.FiberTree.get_event_handler( view.fiber_tree, fiber_id_str, handler_index ) case handler do nil -> {:error, {:stale_handler, ref}} fun when is_function(fun, 0) -> fun.() {:ok, flush_messages(view)} fun when is_function(fun, 1) -> fun.(params) {:ok, flush_messages(view)} end _ -> {:error, {:bad_ref_format, ref}} end end defp dispatch_event(_view, ref, _params) do {:error, {:not_filament_event, ref}} end defp flush_messages(view) do receive do {:filament_set_state, fiber_id, slot_index, new_value} -> view = apply_hook_slot_update(view, fiber_id, slot_index, new_value) flush_messages(view) {:filament_observable_update, fiber_id, slot_index, new_value} -> view = apply_hook_slot_update(view, fiber_id, slot_index, new_value) flush_messages(view) {:filament_observable_resubscribe, fiber_id, slot_index} -> view = apply_hook_slot_update(view, fiber_id, slot_index, :needs_resubscribe) flush_messages(view) after 0 -> rerender(view) end end defp apply_hook_slot_update(view, fiber_id, slot_index, new_value) do tree = Filament.FiberTree.update_hook_slot( view.fiber_tree, fiber_id, slot_index, fn _ -> new_value end ) %{view | fiber_tree: tree} end defp rerender(view) do # Re-render the component with the current fiber_tree state. # Check Filament.Reconciler.update/3 or update/4 actual signature in # lib/filament/reconciler.ex and call it here with the updated fiber_tree. # The intent: given updated hook_slots (from state changes), re-run render/1 # on the component and produce new rendered output. case Filament.Reconciler.update(view.component, view.props, view.fiber_tree, %{ owner_pid: view.owner_pid, observable_stubs: view.stubs }) do {:ok, new_fiber_tree, new_rendered} -> html = rendered_to_string(new_rendered) %{view | fiber_tree: new_fiber_tree, rendered: new_rendered, rendered_html: html} {:error, reason} -> raise "Filament.Test rerender failed: #{inspect(reason)}" end end end ``` NOTE on Reconciler.update: adapt the call to match the actual signature in `lib/filament/reconciler.ex`. Pass `owner_pid` and `observable_stubs` in whatever context argument the reconciler accepts. If the reconciler does not accept an `observable_stubs` context, that is a deviation — stop and comment. --- ## 2. Add Floki test dependency FILE: filament/mix.exs Add `:floki` as a test-only dependency if not already present: ```elixir {:floki, ">= 0.30.0", only: :test} ``` Check `mix.exs` first — it may already be a transitive dependency of LiveView. If it is already present (check `mix.lock` or `mix deps`), do not add a duplicate. --- ## 3. Tests FILE: test/filament/test_test.exs ```elixir defmodule Filament.TestTest do use ExUnit.Case, async: true import Filament.Test # Minimal component for testing — defined here, not imported from examples defmodule CounterComp do use Filament.Component defcomponent do prop :initial, :integer, default: 0 def render(assigns) do {count, set_count} = use_state(@initial) ~F"""
Count: {count}
""" end end end defmodule ObservableComp do use Filament.Component defcomponent do prop :server, :term, required: true def render(assigns) do value = use_observable(@server) ~F"""
{value}
""" end end end end ``` Test cases: 1. **mount returns rendered HTML** — mount CounterComp with %{initial: 0}, assert render_text contains "Count: 0" 2. **click updates state and re-renders** — mount, click "button", assert render_text contains "Count: 1"; click again, assert "Count: 2" 3. **has_class? true** — render a component with `class="active"` on a div, assert `has_class?(view, "div", "active")` is true 4. **has_class? false** — assert `has_class?(view, "div", "missing")` is false 5. **has_class? raises on missing selector** — assert raises when selector not found 6. **stub observable injected at mount** — mount ObservableComp with `stub: [{:my_server, fn _req -> 42 end}]` passing `:my_server` as the server prop, assert render_text contains "42" 7. **stub push updates rendered output** — mount with stub, push new value via Filament.Test.Stub.push/2, then simulate a re-render trigger, assert new value shown 8. **click on nonexistent selector** — assert click returns {:error, {:no_element, _}} 9. **submit delivers params to handler** — component renders a form with on_submit, call submit(view, "form", %{"name" => "Alice"}), assert handler received params Run: `mix test test/filament/test_test.exs` --- ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `Filament.Test.mount/3` compiles and returns {:ok, view} - [ ] `render_text/1`, `has_class?/3`, `click/2`, `submit/3` all implemented - [ ] Floki dep present (add if needed) - [ ] All 9 tests pass - [ ] Dialyzer clean - [ ] Track B/C/D/E test suites still pass (no regressions)
title: F1: Filament.Test — Rung 2 isolated component test API (mount, click, submit, render_text, has_class?)
